newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA'S JOHNSON PONDERS RETURN TO DERBY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA'S JOHNSON PONDERS RETURN TO DERBY.

text.p: Aston Villa striker Tommy Johnson will decide this weekend whether to return to his former club Derby County for 2.0 million pounds ($3.2 million).
The two premier league sides have agreed a transfer fee but Johnson, who left Derby for Villa two years ago, had yet to agree personal terms, a Derby spokeswoman said.
"Tommy's taking the weekend to think about it," she said. "The fee's been decided upon but he hasn't agreed personal terms so he won't be able to play at the weekend."
Earlier reports said Johnson had already signed for Derby, who were trying to complete all the necessary paperwork in time to allow him to face Everton in a league match on Saturday.
Derby would have to pay Villa more than the initial 2.0 million pound fee if Johnson helped them to avoid relegation, although they could not reveal how much more.
"We've sealed the deal with Villa and there'll be more to pay if we stay up,'' manager Jim Smith said.

Johnson, 26, joined Aston Villa in a 2.9 million pound ($4.6 million) deal which also involved Gary Charles and he scored 15 goals in 67 appearances for them. In his previous spell at Derby he scored 41 goals in 129 appearances.
Villa manager Brian Little said: "It's a good deal for us and if it's right for Tommy, that's fine."
